title: Shared intrinsic Mirror view with sparse private residuals
hypothesis: For a mixed task bank with one common aligned two-dimensional function plus sparse task-private intrinsic residuals, replacing the common two-coefficient address with one Mirror angle will reduce actual serialized payload by at least 10% versus the same shared/private decomposition with direct common coefficients, while meeting held-out quality. This should outperform simply increasing a global intrinsic dimension when private residual density is low.
physical_object: one 32D linear base predictor and deterministic 32x16 random orthonormal intrinsic basis shared across tasks
mirror_coordinate: one FP16 angle/task over a shared-radius first two basis columns; sparse private residuals store intrinsic coordinate indices plus FP16 values
logical_multiplicity: 128 task functions with a common orbit component and task-specific sparse residuals; task count is not independent capacity
controls: shared direct two-coefficient address plus identical sparse private residuals

task.private_residual_groups: 48 tasks with 0 private values; 32 with 2; 32 with 4; 16 with 8, on randomly selected coordinates 2..15
task.shared_orbit: first two intrinsic coordinates have fixed radius 0.25 and per-task uniform angle

fresh.access_condition: Source, controls, generation, metric, byte gate and decision rule frozen before fresh execution.

training.optimizer: least squares for direct coefficients and sparse private values; fixed 720-point grid for angle fitting

storage.authority: actual deterministic serialized inference payload bytes after reload
paid_objects: common direct coefficients or Mirror angles

gates.promising: All fresh seeds: Mirror actual payload <=0.90x shared-direct+sparse-residual control; mean normalized held-out MSE <=1e-4 and within 1e-5 of direct control; report fixed-dimension and private-count frontier.
gates.fail: Mirror payload >= direct shared/private control in >=2 fresh seeds, or quality misses in >=2 fresh seeds.
gates.not_established: Any serialization, split-integrity, or deterministic replay mismatch.

boundaries: teacher explicitly shares a fixed-radius orbit
sparse private indices are supplied by task fitting
no learned router, continual optimizer, language model, or capacity claim
